items.title: TRIDENT and SHAKTI: A Framework and Benchmark for Hindi AI-Text Detection
items.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly multilingual, distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text is essential for maintaining information integrity. However, research remains English-centric, with limited benchmarks for low-resource languages such as Hindi. To address this gap, we introduce SHAKTI, a large-scale Hindi benchmark covering four genres, eight LLM families, multiple prompting strategies, and adversarial transformations. We evaluate its quality through human annotation and analyze linguistic, grammatical, and sentiment-based differences between human- and AI-generated texts. Building on these findings, we propose TRIDENT, a round-trip translation-based detection framework with three variants: TRIDENT-S (static threshold), TRIDENT-D (dynamic threshold), and TRIDENT-C (logistic regression using multi-distance RTT features). TRIDENT leverages semantic consistency between original and round-trip translated texts to identify AI-generated content. Extensive experiments show that TRIDENT outperforms conventional and supervised baselines, with TRIDENT-S achieving the best overall performance. Further evaluations across seven languages, adversarial settings, and unseen LLMs demonstrate its multilingual applicability and robustness, while highlighting sensitivity to the translation model.

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. We attribute this failure to a fundamental modality mismatch: reasoning is performed in a discrete token space, whereas image generation operates in a continuous space. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Latent Reasoning framework in Continuous space (LARC), which alleviates the token-level bottleneck by reasoning over continuous hidden states. Specifically, the training framework consists of two stages: (i) curriculum supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and (ii) information-gain reinforcement learning (RL). First, the curriculum SFT stage gradually converts token-level reasoning into latent reasoning. Subsequently, the information-gain RL stage self-evolves latent reasoning without ground truth supervision. Experiments across diverse text-to-image generation benchmarks show that LARC consistently improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity. items.summary: In real-world deployments, large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly evolving from single-model invocation toward heterogeneous deployments in which different models are dynamically invoked for inference. When the same context is reused across models, however, each newly selected target model typically has to process it again, repeatedly incurring substantial computational costs. Therefore, we propose ACCT (Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer), which targets KV cache transfer between models of different scales within the same model family. ACCT transforms the KV cache produced by a source model into sparse KV states that can be directly consumed by a target model, thereby enabling cross-model reuse of context computation and decoupling context computation from downstream inference. The target model can therefore perform inference using the transferred KV without reprocessing the original context. items.summary: The quadratic scaling of attention is a fundamental bottleneck limiting the long-context capabilities of large language models (LLMs). A variety of approaches have attempted to circumvent this, but they either fail to match attention's expressiveness (e.g., sliding-window or linear attention variants with fixed-size state) or only achieve constant-factor speedups (e.g., sparse attention methods whose indexers themselves scale quadratically). In this paper, we derive an asymptotically subquadratic sparse attention method based on a hierarchical, tree-structured indexer, which we call Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA). ZHA constructs a tree of recursively compressed key summaries over the KV cache, which future queries traverse from the top down to retrieve a sparse subset of keys. Crucially, by iteratively growing the tree's depth, the total cost including routing and final attention grows sublinearly in sequence length, resulting in overall subquadratic (but superlinear) scaling for attention. We demonstrate that ZHA can be cheaply applied to existing pretrained models with only a short KL distillation training stage over a few billion tokens, and maintains performance on long-context retrieval and challenging reasoning, mathematical, and agentic coding evaluation tasks. items.summary: This paper presents a robust and imperceptible watermarking scheme for DICOM medical images that integrates the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) with a Denoising Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). In the proposed scheme, each DICOM slice is segmented to isolate its Region of Interest (ROI), which is then partitioned into equal-sized blocks and transformed into the frequency domain using the block Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). A chaotic Duffing map generates a secret key that determines the candidate blocks used for embedding, while the WOA optimizes the per-slice quantization step of a Quantization-Index-Modulation (QIM) embedding to minimize the average Mean Squared Error (MSE) while preserving robustness, thereby achieving the best trade-off between imperceptibility and robustness. items.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
items.summary: Agentic workflows are increasingly shifting towards long-horizon tasks, such as open-ended scientific work, where models benefit from long context windows. However, at ultra-long context (above 1M tokens), full attention is prohibitively expensive. A promising approach is sparse attention, in which a dedicated indexer selects a subset of keys for the attention. Yet current methods of indexing either still have quadratic cost in context size or lose accuracy at ultra-long context scale. We address this with Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), an efficient attention method that maintains accuracy at ultra-long context. In LSA, keys are hierarchically clustered in a learned latent space, and queries score the hierarchy of clusters instead of scoring every key, making prefill, decode and training faster at long context. We propose two variants, Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), which can be applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), which is trained natively on the next-token loss alone. On GLM-5.3-FLASH (QWEN-3.8-27B) at 10M tokens, D-LSA speeds up one attention layer by 22.7x (72.4x) in prefill and 4.6x (42.5x) in decode over its original sparse attention (full attention), while keeping similar accuracy across a variety of tasks. items.title: ZERA: A Loop-Skipping Mechanism for Sparsity-Aware RISC-V Multicore Accelerator
items.summary: Deep Neural Networks exhibit high sparsity, yet conventional RISC-V-based architectures remain inefficient by processing zero-valued operands as a useful value, resulting in sub-optimal throughput. This paper presents ZERA, a sparsityaware RISC-V multi-core architecture featuring a Zero-Detected ISA and a hardware-integrated loop-skipping mechanism. By utilizing a Zero Mask Memory (ZMM) and a Hardware Loop Engine (HWE), ZERA collapses entire innermost loop iterations into single-cycle skips provided that the loop iteration comprises a multiplication by zero. If not, conventional data flow is executed, ensuring ZERA provides consistent speedup for both dense and sparse operands. Prototyped on an AMD Kria KV260, an 8-PE ZERA cluster achieves an average speedup of 3.4× at 90% sparsity over conventional execution without zero optimization, acted as a baseline, incurring only a 7% hardware overhead. A SqueezeNet-1D case study for intrusion detection demonstrates a 2.30× speedup over a baseline while maintaining 86.34% accuracy, significantly outperforming general-purpose processors like the ARM Cortex-A53 in execution efficiency ranging from 1.1× to 4.65× speed improvement.

items.title: Input-dependent Neuromodulation Enhances Mixed-Signal Neuromorphic Hardware
items.summary: Gating mechanisms allow a fixed neural network to adapt its computation to the current input by dynamically modulating its effective parameters. In the brain, neuromodulation uses this principle to move neural circuits between dynamical regimes, and deep learning exploits input-dependent gating, e.g., in gated recurrent networks and self-attention. Input-dependent modulation has also recently been shown to improve spiking neural networks, with particularly strong benefits in small, parameter-limited ones. This makes neuromodulation especially promising for neuromorphic processors at the edge, where area, memory and energy budgets constrain network size, while circuit physics limits parameter precision. Here we demonstrate input-dependent, within-trial neuromodulation of a spiking recurrent neural network on a mixed-signal neuromorphic processor. An off-chip modulator reads the on-chip network's input and activity and adjusts its population-level gains while the chip's analog circuits compute with the physics of the silicon. Neuromodulation raises binary spoken-digit classification accuracy by $+17.3 \pm 10.4$ percentage points, tested across five hardware network instantiations.

items.title: Natural Language Processing for Interactive Learning Experiences
items.summary: Natural Language Processing (NLP) has become a core component for next generation e-learning ecosystems, especially in content delivery. It enables platforms to understand, respond and adapt to individual learners. With the rise of deep learning models especially transformer based architectures, NLP now offers state of the art capabilities for real-time interaction, personalized feedback, and adaptive learning pathways. This chapter examines NLP-driven systems powered by deep learning to enhance learner engagement, motivation, and cognitive development. It is developed by converting static educational materials into dynamic, conversational, and highly interactive experiences. The key ideas in this chapter includes understanding text, language models that can generate responses, intelligent tutoring systems, automatic grading, feedback that considers emotions, and learning that uses multiple types of media (such as text, audio, and images). Practical use cases and emerging research trends are highlighted. Ethical, pedagogical and technological challenges are also discussed.

WellLog-LLM combines Dynamic Feature Selection with supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and Group Relative Context Optimization (GRCO). items.title: Dual-Counterfactual Evidence Decomposition and Selective Editing for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Abstract Large vision-language models (LVLMs) often generate fluent but visually unsupported content. Existing training-free methods mainly recalibrate output distributions or edit representations without identifying whether the evidence behind the current claim is visual, linguistic, or shared. This limits intervention precision: unsupported language priors may survive, whereas grounded visual information may be weakened. We introduce a dual-counterfactual evidence decomposition and selective editing framework. Paired visual and linguistic counterfactuals act as sample-specific evidence probes, whose hidden-state responses are decomposed into shared, visual-exclusive, and linguistic-exclusive components. A claim-aware gate attenuates unsupported linguistic evidence only for visually verifiable claims, while an evidence-preserving update protects shared and visual-exclusive support. The method is training-free and requires neither parameter updates nor external verification models. items.title: Intelligent Energy Systems
items.summary: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.

items.title: Foundations of Reinforcement Learning and Control: Connections and New Perspectives
items.summary: Reinforcement learning and control theory are two adjacent scientific fields that focus on optimizing the controller of unknown dynamical systems using feedback. While both fields have common roots in dynamic programming, they have evolved with distinct methodologies, goals, and cultures. Despite decades of mutual influence, a significant gap persists between the two communities. This tutorial introduces adaptive control, actor-critic reinforcement algorithms, and a new way to combine these two paradigms for data-driven decision making on a classical locomotion control problem. Our aim is to provide a foundation for understanding the core differences between the two approaches and insights to help experts in each field better understand and engage with the tools and approaches of the other.

items.title: Integrating Transformer Neural Processes and Deep Kernel Learning for High-Throughput Screening and Uncertainty Quantification for Water-Splitting Electrocatalysts Across Perovskites and Metal Alloys
items.summary: Years of experimentation have failed to enable the prediction of an efficient electrocatalyst from either a perovskite or an alloy without weeks of experimentation. There are more than a million perovskites, more exponential number of alloys but fewer than 0.1% of them have been studied. The traditional approach has failed. Density Functional Theory is impractical because of costs. Gaussian Process Regression struggles with scalability and lacks transfer between families. Its uncertainty calibration is off by miles. More importantly, the literature is not homogenous. Any framework that ignores that problem learns procedures, not physics. We gather Transformer Neural Processes (meta-learning across families) with Deep Kernel Learning (statistical uncertainty). This neural architecture can scale and model overpotential, stability, and activity with correlated uncertainties. Standardization of overpotential is done through Tafel correction. Prediction errors in the range of 50 millivolts and two- to three-fold reduction of experiments through Bayesian Optimization are our goals.

items.title: FOLLIE: Automated Reasoning over the First Dataset of Sentences with their First-Order Logical Representation for French
items.summary: FOLLIE (for First-Order Logic for Language Inference and Entailment for French) connects French sentences, compositional first-order representations and automated natural language inference (NLI). The first French NLI-ready, NL-to-FOL resource, it contains 19,983 inference records and 36,987 non-empty sentence-slot--formula mappings from six heterogeneous NLI sources, retaining French lexical material and source problem structure. Its silver annotations are produced by a neural--symbolic pipeline, with 111 separately identified LLM-assisted additions. The construction combines morphosyntactic analysis, probability-conditioned categorial multitagging, grammatical proof search, discourse representation and first-order semantic construction. Stage-wise experiments show substantial gains in derivation coverage; analyses of conjunction distributions, logical-operator incidence and scope alternation characterise the resulting resource. We then develop an automatic inference engine whose input-conditioned background theories address lexical relations, quantification, quantities, event structure and temporal dependencies. Prover9 supplies proofs for entailment and contradiction, while Mace4 supports bounded consistency checks. Three-way accuracies are 65.37% on all 335 FraCaS-FR problems, 70.33% on 300 GQNLI-FR problems and 71.35% on 9,399 eligible SICK-FR records pooled across splits.

items.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. items.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. items.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
items.summary: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape recommendations across chatbots, e-commerce, and user-generated content (UGC) platforms, creating demand for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to improve item visibility in generated responses. items.summary: Predicting stock returns requires modeling persistent company relations and time-varying market signals. items.title: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture
items.summary: RISC-V based AI accelerators have become popular and not only for AI and ML, but also as vehicles for exploring HPC workloads more generally. Tenstorrent are one example, and whilst they document their Tensix architecture in detail and develop their software stack openly, running code has historically required a physical card, and their recently released simulator targets hardware equivalence rather than introspection. In this paper we present Wolfpine, a community developed RISC-V simulator for the Tensix architecture, supporting both the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating seamlessly with the TT-Metal software stack. Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. items.title: Graph-Mediated Large Language Model Systems in the Agentic Era: Reasoning, Knowledge, Retrieval, Execution, and Coordination
items.summary: Graphs play an increasingly important role in large language model (LLM) systems, supporting structural reasoning, knowledge grounding, retrieval, and memory. As these systems evolve toward the agentic era, graphs also organize execution dependencies and multi-agent communication, linking intermediate observations and retained information to subsequent decisions. However, understanding their contribution requires distinguishing the function of each graph operation, the component responsible for its computation, and the subsequent use of its output. This survey introduces an operation-level role--locus taxonomy for reasoning, knowledge and evidence, retrieval and memory, execution, and coordination. We compare how graph observations and external computations guide decisions, how memory representations and updates support later tasks, and how dependencies constrain execution and information delivery. These comparisons distinguish improvements in local metrics from downstream task performance while retaining the conditions under which results were reported. We then organize benchmarks, comparison designs, process diagnostics, and system costs into an evaluation framework. Finally, we identify open challenges in adaptive computation and stopping, memory maintenance, and dependency-aware recovery. items.title: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
items.summary: RL for LLM reasoning often reaches an early performance plateau as the policy distribution becomes increasingly sharp. Recent work has studied policy entropy as both a diagnostic and a control signal for this behavior. In our experiments, however, increasing entropy alone does not reliably change the eventual plateau. We analyze RL through its implicit target policy and derive a sharpness factor $κ$, together with an effective counterpart $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$, that describes how strongly reward or advantage gaps are translated into probability-ratio gaps. Motivated by this view, we introduce \emph{reward budgeting}, a plug-in advantage construction that assigns a fixed total reward budget to each prompt. For binary rewards and independent on-policy rollouts, its unclipped score-function estimator follows the gradient of an exact finite-$G$ concave objective with diminishing returns, while its advantage gap decreases as more rollouts become correct. For general rewards, a shifted log-mean interpretation holds asymptotically under the stated regularity conditions. These results motivate, rather than establish exact objective equivalence for, the clipped implementations. On Qwen3-8B and Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, reward budgeting consistently improves a range of RL baselines, with gains up to +12.50 on AMC23 and +10.00 on AIME24 and AIME25. items.title: Exploring Model Invariance with Discrete Search for Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization
items.summary: As language models continue to grow in size due to their success in a wide range of applications such as conversational agents and coding, there is a pressing need to make them more accessible. A popular technique is to reduce their memory footprint by post-training quantization, where we use fewer bits (e.g., 4--8 bits) to represent the model without retraining it. However, quantizing language models remains a challenging task, especially in the ultra-low-bit setup (e.g., 2 bits). In this paper, we propose InvarExplore, a unified framework that systematically explores different kinds of model invariance to maximize quantization performance. Importantly, InvarExplore features a discrete search algorithm that enables us to explore permutation invariance, which is under-studied as it cannot be optimized with gradient-based methods. Such exploration allows us to take advantage of the synergy between each type of invariance. Our results and in-depth analyses show that InvarExplore is compatible with existing state-of-the-art integer quantization methods, achieving an add-on performance improvement over strong competing methods.

items.title: OneMall: One Architecture, More Scenarios — End-to-End Generative Recommender Family for E-commerce
items.summary: In the wave of generative recommendation, we present OneMall, an end-to-end generative recommendation framework tailored for e-commerce services at Kuaishou. Our OneMall systematically unifies the e-commerce's multiple item distribution scenarios, such as Product-card, short-video and live-streaming. Specifically, it comprises three key components, aligning the entire model training pipeline to the LLM's pre-training/post-training: (1)E-commerce Semantic Tokenizer : we provide a tokenizer solution that captures both real-world semantics and business-specific item relations across different scenarios; (2)Transformer-based Architecture : we largely utilize Transformer as our model backbone, e.g., employing Query-Former for long sequence compression, Cross-Attention for multi-behavior sequence fusion, and Sparse MoE for scalable auto-regressive generation; (3)Reinforcement Learning Pipeline: we further connect retrieval and ranking models via RL, enabling the ranking model to serve as a reward signal for end-to-end policy retrieval model optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OneMall achieves consistent improvements across all e-commerce scenarios: +14.7% GMV in Product-Card, +10.3% GMV in Short-Video, and +4.9% GMV in Live-Streaming. OneMall has been deployed, serving over 400 million daily active users at Kuaishou.

items.title: Fully homomorphic encryption on LlaMA 3 model for partial privacy preserving LLM inference
items.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence applications have delivered significant improvements in service efficiency and language understanding. However, the surge in Large Language Model deployment raises critical security and privacy concerns regarding data exposure and unauthorized access to sensitive information. Quantum computing attacks pose an imminent threat to existing cryptographic protections, necessitating post-quantum cryptographic approaches. We present a partially privacy-preserving inference pipeline for LLaMA-3 by integrating fully homomorphic encryption into the transformer’s Multi-Query Attention mechanism. Our approach encrypts attention weights and computations across all 32 decoder layers of LLaMA-3.2-3B using lattice-based cryptography via the concrete-ml library, while feed-forward sublayers, layer normalization, and output projections remain in plaintext, a deliberate trade-off achieving practical feasibility on commodity CPUs. Evaluation on the instruction-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B model yields: (i) strong semantic preservation (BERTScore-F1 ∼ 84.4%), (ii) controlled perplexity degradation (1.18 FP16 vs. 2.09 FHE), (iii) competitive BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L scores ( ∼ 35.6% and ∼ 51.8%), (iv) downstream GLUE benchmark accuracy, and (v) 825 ms latency at 17 tokens/second on AMD EPYC CPUs. We further present quantization-aware FHE and quantization bit-width ablation studies

items.title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
items.summary: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models, covering 1D and 2D hierarchical representations combined with 32-bit, 8-bit, and binary quantization, for 168 configurations per task. We report each efficiency dimension separately: theoretical per-vector storage and end-to-end evaluation time. Under a Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis, int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking and costs at most 1.5 percentage points overall, whereas binary quantization is significantly worse across every task category. Halving the embedding dimension once is not statistically detectable above $m=16$; two successive halvings always are. Combining an 8x dimensionality reduction with int8 yields a 32x reduction in per-vector storage at 94.4% of baseline effectiveness. Because evaluation times were measured once, we treat them as indicative: we find no evidence that quantization speeds up evaluation, whereas sampling from intermediate layers shortens it substantially. items.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six model--size settings, 29 of 36 submissions pass verification. Selecting the lowest-perplexity agent design per task yields an average 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy, compared with 79.56% for BF16. Recorded experiments reveal how agents achieve these outcomes and where improvement breaks down. Agents lower PPL in 21 of 24 revisions at nearly fixed storage; complete-model feedback reverses 17 of 79 prior local rankings; and generation and inference tests expose failures that likelihood alone misses. items.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
items.summary: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution. At intermediate generation steps in few-step sampling, student-score estimation can be difficult, and commonly used estimators may describe a different distribution from the one used to update the student. Flow matching allows a more flexible approach to supervision through velocity fields constructed from the student's sampling process. Building on this perspective, we introduce Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), which uses a learned critic to compare student and teacher fields and turn their disagreement into feedback for learning. VAD unifies score distillation, Fisher-based matching, and moment matching, also explaining existing heuristic MMD updates and delivering new training objectives. We further develop VA-TDM, which follows trajectory distribution matching: providing supervision for partial denoising along the student trajectory. Beyond this, VA-TDM combines transition-aware online velocity learning and dual-form VAD supervision across intermediate student transitions. items.title: Granular Framework for Construction Material Price Forecasting: Econometric and Machine-Learning Approaches
items.summary: Abstract The persistent volatility of construction material prices poses significant risks to cost estimation, budgeting, and project delivery, underscoring the urgent need for granular and scalable forecasting methods. items.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
items.summary: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. items.title: CacheGraft: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Latent-Space Document Enrichment
items.summary: Recent work in machine learning has demonstrated that transformer-based language model agents can communicate state not only through text, but also directly in latent space via key-value (KV) caches. In this paper, we argue that such cache-to-cache translation can provide utility beyond the original motivating application of real-time agent communication and can instead be utilized for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Building on the Cache-to-Cache (C2C) fusion framework, our proposed system CacheGraft encodes each corpus passage offline into a fused KV cache representation between a larger sharer model (4B parameters in our experiments) and a smaller receiver model (0.6B parameters) such that this cache can be injected into the receiver at query time with no need for the larger model. Across five QA benchmarks and two independent locally-run judges, CacheGraft improves answer quality over the text-only receiver baseline in 29 out of 30 comparisons, of which 17 of the 30 are statistically significant. Notably, these gains are zero-shot with respect to the fuser, which was never trained on retrieval data. These initial results suggest that latent-space document enrichment may be a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of RAG systems, particularly in compute-constrained settings where it is only feasible to deploy a small model at inference time.

items.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
items.summary: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBen

items.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
items.summary: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. A single multimodal judge evaluates six dimensions of communication and design, with three repeated judgments per figure. We attempt source-constrained revisions of all 371 figures, of which 369 pass the recorded fidelity checks. Original-figure ratings show no uniform decline across periods. Revisions increase mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and decrease aesthetic coherence ratings by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. Gains in the six-dimension average are larger for main-sample motivation figures than for frameworks. Case analyses show that added explanation can clarify comparisons while leaving typographic hierarchy and visual economy unresolved. These model-based findings support researcher-led design, with AI assisting exploration and authors retaining responsibility for explanatory purpose, composition, and scientific relationships. items.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
items.summary: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video learning, making metric motion usable as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target. Cross-stream action-video coupling establishes close correspondence between metric motion and visual dynamics through lightweight adaptation while preserving the pretrained visual prior. Together, these designs establish a generalist framework spanning five action-video tasks. Despite adaptation only on controlled laboratory recordings, EgoGeneralist generalizes to diverse unseen scenes and interactions with effective action control and visual quality, bridging pretrained visual knowledge and metric 3D human motion.

items.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
items.summary: Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Its guide has three replaceable parts (slots), an organ segmenter, a controller and a reward, which received 20 published methods, each run on the same 60 episodes of six held-out patients. A pose oracle, reading the exact probe pose available only in simulation, set the reference. The results below are exploratory. Results: On these CTs, the probe started on average 16.0 mm from the target view; the pose oracle brought it to 1.5 mm. Of the results known when the combination was fixed, only an image-similarity reward (SSIM) was slightly but detectably better, so the combination was our guide with that reward. items.title: An Image Is Worth K Topics: A Visual Structural Topic Model with Pretrained Image Embeddings
items.summary: Abstract Political scientists are increasingly interested in analyzing visual content at scale. However, the existing computational toolbox is still in need of methods and models attuned to the specific challenges and goals of social and political inquiry. In this article, we introduce a visual structural topic model (vSTM) that combines continuous image embeddings with a structural topic model. This has important advantages compared to existing approaches. First, continuous embeddings allow the model to capture the semantic complexity of images, which is relevant to the study of politics. A consequence of using continuous embeddings is that we can directly use off-the-shelf pretrained deep learning models, offering state-of-the-art performance in image analysis tasks while saving time, cost and resources. Second, the structural topic model provides the ability to analyze how topics and covariates are related, while maintaining a nuanced representation of images as a mixture of multiple topics. In our experiments, we show that the vSTM is able to identify topics that are interpretable, coherent and relevant to the study of online political communication.

items.title: A professionally developed visual coding framework for affective video analysis
items.summary: Introduction Affective responses to videos arise from multidimensional, context-dependent visual features that unfold over time. However, no standardized method exists to characterize these features, limiting research on visual-based immersive interventions and broader computer vision science. We developed an expert-informed visual coding framework to provide a systematic approach to visual coding. Methods A visual coding framework was developed by film professionals to characterize cinematographic features that may be relevant to viewers’ emotional responses. items.title: ConnectionMind: Leveraging Social Networks and Large Language Models for Personalized Recommendation at Meta
items.summary: Modern recommendation systems on social media platforms such as Meta must model complex social relationships alongside massive and heterogeneous content such as text and video. Traditional recommendation models, however, often omit these signals or treat them independently, limiting their ability to integrate multi-relational context for fine-grained personalization. We present ConnectionMind, a production-ready recommendation framework that tightly integrates social network structure with large language models (LLMs) to enable scalable and reasoning-aware personalization at Meta. ConnectionMind constructs a heterogeneous graph connecting users, items, friends, groups, and creator pages, and formulates recommendation as a graph reasoning problem that discovers personalized paths from users to candidate items. An LLM-based policy reasons over these graph structures to guide recommendation decisions. To train the system at scale, ConnectionMind adopts a two-stage strategy: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on large-scale user--item interaction trajectories to initialize the reasoning policy, followed by end-to-end reinforcement learning (RL) to further optimize personalized graph reasoning. items.title: A Framework for Guaranteed Active Fault Diagnosis with Applications to Aircraft Systems
items.summary: Within the multiple-model framework, active fault diagnosis applies auxiliary control input signals to ex?cite the system such that fault modes are distinguishable. For aircraft systems, it has been pointed out by some rele?vant works that certain faults cannot be effectively detected and isolated in time without actively exciting the aircraft dynamics. However, existing works have not simultane?ously addressed the optimal auxiliary control design with theoretical guarantees and the FDI method with an effective mechanism for triggering the active fault diagnosis. Hence, we are motivated to propose a framework of active FDI for aircraft systems to explicitly address the aforementioned issue. Specifically, we first formulate a receding-horizon FDI scheme for estimating the likelihood of candidate fault modes with proved effectiveness, and then we propose a method for estimating mode probabilities, based on which a mechanism is designed for triggering auxiliary control for active fault diagnosis. The auxiliary control signal design is formulated such that the effectiveness for FDI is theoret?ically guaranteed and the disruption to nominal flight oper?ation is minimized. Numerical test results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

items.title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics
items.summary: This extended abstract discusses a specific and, in our experience, practically relevant role for large language models (LLMs) in underwater robotics. Our main premise is that, in underwater fielding missions, the immediate difficulty is often not the synthesis of new low-level control laws, but the operation of complex robotic systems under limited communications, partial observability, and expensive field time. In particular, a significant fraction of the effort during sea trials is devoted to fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination across heterogeneous assets and operators. We argue that LLMs may be useful at this higher operational level, especially when grounded in structured vehicle state, alarms, logs, mission context, and existing planning or validation tools. items.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things in Education and Cultural Studies
items.summary: Abstract AI and IoT add most value in education and cultural studies if they expand who is reached and protected, and our simulations suggest that they may narrow that reach almost as easily. This paper (i) synthesizes the literature on AI (Artificial Intelligence) and the Internet of Things (IoT) across teaching and learning, assessment, campus operations, digital humanities, and heritage preservation, and (ii) evaluates two representative applications with reproducible Monte Carlo models. The first is an early-warning system that directs limited tutoring capacity to at-risk students, with an explicit equity metric for a minority group whose data are less informative. The second is IoT microclimate monitoring in a heritage gallery with three alarm strategies. items.summary: Abstract Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of applications.However, as their deployment becomes increasingly widespread, recent studies have revealed that VLMs are vulnerable to visual jailbreak attacks, where adversarially manipulated images induce safety-aligned models to produce harmful responses, posing serious threats to real-world security.Input purification defenses must balance perturbation suppression against content preservation; a fixed transformation strength may be unsuitable for inputs and attacks with different characteristics.We propose FASDP, a Frequency-Aware Scale-Diverse Purification framework that adaptively allocates purification strength per image.It fuses multi-scale candidates from a single frozen denoiser using low-frequency consistency modulated by a self-referenced frequency cue.The framework requires no task-specific training or access to the target model.We evaluate FASDP on LLaVA-1.5-7B, InstructBLIP-7B, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B under three representative pixel-space attacks.FASDP attains strong protection under these attacks while keeping clean-image performance on downstream tasks close to that of the undefended models.

items.title: Legal Ethics of Generative Artificial Intelligence Training Data Usage in Large Language Models: Copyright and Personal Data Perspective
items.summary: This research originates from security and privacy risks associated with Generative AI Large Language Models (LLMs), especially concerning data used for training in relation to Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) and Personal Data Protection (PDP). The study seeks to examine existing regulatory guidance and develop a national framework that protects user privacy and IPR. The method employs normative legal research using statutory and conceptual approaches, by reviewing the legal frameworks of Indonesia, South Korea, the European Union (EU), and Japan, along with direct testing of LLM prompts. The findings show that LLMs continuously absorb users’ input prompts, data, and corrections to support deeper model training, thereby revealing significant security vulnerabilities under PDP laws. Moreover, in the absence of strong human creative control and predictability, each incoming data item may potentially breach privacy and copyright laws and may also damage original creators. Therefore, legal governance should move toward explicit licensing, fair compensation, and technical verification standards such as provenance labeling. The study concludes that mandatory human-centric supervision, explicit user consent, and freedom of choice are essential legal limits. items.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.summary: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. Our objective is to maximise the cosine similarity of a supplied residual stream direction with the activations of the text generated by the MAEM. This label-free RL objective helps to scale MAEMs on diverse sources of residual stream directions. Empirically, we find the resultant metamodel produces informative exemplars: a Qwen3.6-27B MAEM inverts held-out activations better than corpus search or a natural-language autoencoder (NLA), beats corpus search (at 10M tokens) on a majority of held-out languages/domains, and activates 89% of held-out SAE features. It also identifies concepts behind steering vectors about as well as NLAs, recovers the payloads of LoRA backdoors more often than corpus search, and can even verbalise some model workspace inner monologue. Unlike explanations produced by other metamodels (e.g. NLAs), MAEM exemplars can be verified with a forward pass on the subject model, making the MAEM objective a grounded alternative for scaling the training of metamodels.

items.title: Direct-Access-Enabled GPU Memory Offloading with Optimal Efficiency for LLM Inference
items.summary: LLM inference is constrained by GPU memory capacity and bandwidth. Tiered memory architectures mitigate this by allowing the GPU to offload memory to the remote tier. However, existing memory offloading frameworks rely on prefetching data into local GPU HBM. This approach underutilizes system resources by introducing HBM contention, squandering memory capacity, and creating pipeline bubbles. We show that enabling direct GPU access to remote memory significantly outperforms prefetching, achieving optimal aggregate system bandwidth. We propose SplitKernel, an end-to-end direct-access memory offloading framework that uses the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) to asynchronously fetch offloaded weights and KV caches directly from remote memory into GPU shared memory (SMEM). To maximize remote access performance, SplitKernel introduces a greedy algorithm to determine optimal per-operation offloading ratios, alongside active congestion control and TMA multicast to eliminate interconnect bottlenecks and read amplification. Evaluations across diverse architectures show that SplitKernel achieves near-optimal bandwidth aggregation, with up to 7.7× performance gains on NVLink-C2C and 2.3× on PCIe systems compared to state-of-the-art memory offloading baselines.

items.title: A Semi‐automatic Puncture System for Liver Rupture Haemostasis: Ex Vivo and In Vivo Study
items.summary: ABSTRACT Background Liver rupture caused by blunt trauma can result in severe haemorrhage and death. Percutaneous puncture embolisation is a potential minimally invasive approach for haemostasis, but manual puncture is limited by difficult bleeding‐site localization and hand–eye coordination. Methods We developed a semi‐automatic puncture system integrating a robotic arm and a compact rack‐pinion driven end‐effector. Positioning and posture accuracy were evaluated, followed by ex vivo and in vivo porcine liver embolisation experiments. Results The system can achieve mean positioning and posture accuracies of 0.36 mm and 1.03° under load‐free conditions, and 1.83 mm and 2.67° in the soft‐tissue phantom, respectively. Embolic material was delivered to the target region, and cessation of visible bleeding was observed within approximately 20 s in the ex vivo and in vivo experiments. Conclusions The results support the preliminary feasibility of this approach for percutaneous puncture embolisation of complex hepatic lacerations.

items.title: AI for Solar Energy Systems
items.summary: The rapid expansion of solar energy has accelerated the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve forecasting accuracy, photovoltaic performance, intelligent control, fault diagnosis, energy storage management, and smart grid operation. Recent advances in machine learning, deep learning, Digital Twins, Physics-Informed Machine Learning, Edge AI, Federated Learning, and Generative AI have transformed solar energy systems into more adaptive and data-driven infrastructures. Despite these advances, challenges related to data quality, model generalization, computational efficiency, cybersecurity, and explainability continue to limit large-scale deployment. An integrated perspective is presented by connecting AI applications across photovoltaic systems, solar thermal technologies, energy storage, and intelligent energy networks within a unified renewable energy ecosystem. Emerging research trends and future directions highlight the evolution toward AI-native energy systems that support efficient, resilient, and sustainable intelligent societies.

items.title: Natural Language as a User-Facing Representation Language for Robotics

Recent advances suggest a different possible approach: natural language can itself serve as a shared, user-facing representation through which people specify and refine task-relevant knowledge. items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs. The evidence shows that distillation can improve selected quantum students, but benefits are task- and architecture-dependent, and several studies find negligible gains or even performance degradation. Evaluations on physical quantum hardware remain limited, with some testing individual quantum components rather than complete learning pipelines. items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. items.title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. Each decision processes hundreds of visual tokens, often across multiple cameras, leading to substantial computation while allowing irrelevant background content to distract action prediction under distribution shift. We argue that these issues stem from two complementary forms of redundancy: many visual tokens are spatially irrelevant, while attention over the remaining tokens is often misallocated. Based on this observation, we propose T3R, a Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement framework. In the first stage, segmentation-guided token pruning removes irrelevant visual patches to reduce computation and eliminate distracting context. In the second stage, saliency-guided attention biasing reallocates attention toward action-critical visual regions and language instructions within the retained tokens. Together, pruning produces a cleaner candidate set, while attention biasing further emphasizes the most decision-relevant evidence, yielding a better accuracy-efficiency frontier than either stage alone. items.title: Wrist photoplethysmography encodes dietary information
items.summary: Whether wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) contains dietary information remains unknown. We trained a language model on 1.1M meals to predict meal descriptions from PPG, aligning PPG to text. PPG nontrivially predicts meal content; predictability decreases for PPGs farther from meals. This transfers to dietary tasks: PPG increases AUC by 11% for intake and satiety across held-out and independent cohorts, with gains robust to text degradation. Wearable PPG may enable passive dietary monitoring.

items.title: Adaptive Hard Negative Mining for Fine Grained Vision Language Understanding A Negative Result and Analysis
items.summary: Abstract Vision-language models perform well on many multimodal tasks but struggle with fine-grained visual-linguistic reasoning. The SPEC benchmark was introduced to evaluate models on four fine-grained concepts: object size, position, existence, and count. Fine-tuning on SPEC with fixed hard negatives improves baseline performance substantially. This paper asks whether adaptive hard-negative mining, which reweights negatives by their current difficulty, can push performance further. We propose a confusion-weighted training objective and evaluate it on SPEC held-out data. The method underperforms fixed hard-negative training by 23 percentage points on average. We trace the cause to SPEC's design: its candidate sets are uniformly hard, so adaptive reweighting has no difficulty signal to exploit and instead destabilizes training. We also introduce SPEC++, a paired-reasoning diagnostic that combines cases from two SPEC subsets. The fine-tuned model's joint accuracy on SPEC + + equals the product of its individual accuracies, indicating that it treats concepts independently rather than composing them. These two findings serve as cautionary notes for the field: uniform hard negatives are difficult to outperform when the data is designed to be uniformly hard, and high benchmark accuracy should not be read as evidence of compositional understanding.

items.title: A Carbon-Aware IoT Scheduling Framework for Sustainable Smart Homes Using Predictive Energy Models
items.summary: With the widespread popularization of software engineering-based Internet of Things technology, the smart home field has obtained the basic conditions to realize fine-grained monitoring and intelligent control of household energy consumption. Presently, there are two big issues with our home energy management. First, in this paper, our emphasis is only on conserving energy rather than considering whether the energy we consume from the grid is clean or dirty. Second, we are not making sure that the software we use to schedule our energy use is reliable. To address these issues, this study proposes a carbon-aware home energy management framework that integrates predictive modeling, environmentally conscious scheduling, and software reliability validation. The three major entities of the proposed scheme are predicting the closeness, predicting energy usage, and scheduling to utilize energy to reduce our carbon footprint. In this context, utilizing a special formula that considers both energy consumption and carbon emissions, we can find ways to make our homes better and more efficient for the planet. For this newly proposed system, all simulation experiments were completed on the OMNeT++ platform. items.title: An Explainable AI Framework for Real-Time Cyberattack Detection and Risk Assessment
items.summary: As cyberattacks become more sophisticated and more common, detection systems must be not only accurate but also quick and easy to interpret. Although deep learning models have proven to be very effective in detecting intrusion and malware, their black-box nature has hindered their adoption in security operations centers (SOCs), where analysts need to explain and take action on alerts in short timeframes. To offer real-time cyberattack detection with quantitative risk assessment, this paper presents an Explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates a lightweight hybrid deep learning detector with post-hoc and intrinsic explainability methods. The framework combines a Convolutional-Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-BiGRU) architecture for spatio-temporal traffic representation with an attention layer that highlights salient time steps and integrates SHAP (Shapley Additive explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to generate human-readable justifications for every prediction. A dynamic risk-scoring engine then translates detection confidence, feature-level severity, and asset criticality to a normalized risk index that enables prioritized incident response. items.title: Mapping and prioritizing industry 4.0 technologies: an analysis based on patent and scientific publication networks
items.summary: Abstract Industry 4.0 has rapidly evolved since its introduction in 2011, driving global initiatives and promoting the diffusion of enabling technologies, such as IoT, cyber-physical systems, and artificial intelligence. Despite its well-documented benefits, firms face increasing challenges in selecting and integrating multiple​ technologies, particularly amid expanding technological options and uncertainty in implementation pathways. Knowing about this challenge, this study develops a systematic, data-driven methodology to support the prioritization of Industry 4.0 enabling technologies. Drawing on network theory, it analyzes data from scientific publications and patents​ by constructing proximity matrices. A composite index derived from network metrics, combined with a portfolio distance measure, is used to rank and prioritize technologies. The results are benchmarked against real industrial adoption data, highlighting similarities and differences between the approaches, while providing insights on the methodology’s strengths and limitations. Provided that further empirical validation is achieved, the proposed framework holds considerable potential to support managerial decision-making, as well as to be scaled to other technological fields.

items.title: Variation-Resilient Low-Cost PUF with Trust-Based Authentication Implemented in 16 nm FinFET for IoT Security
items.summary: Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) generate unique chip identifiers from manufacturing variations, but transmissions over public networks can be exploited through eavesdropping. To improve variation resilience, the proposed SRPFD-PUF employs bit self-test (BST) for stable-CRP selection, while response-bit tolerance is considered in an illustrative authentication flow. By minimizing additional circuit overhead, strong baseline PUF metrics are maintained at low hardware cost, supporting integration in Internet of Things (IoT) devices. An illustrative PUF-based authentication flow is presented to demonstrate a potential IoT application; end-to-end protocol implementation and security validation remain outside the scope of this study. The three-condition BST screen yields a minimum simulated logarithmic reliability score of 98.93% under the evaluated PVT conditions within 0.675–1.05 V and −40–150 °C. With the circuit architecture and LFSR configuration disclosed, the evaluated machine-learning attacks yield prediction accuracies of 47.68–52.46%, indicating resistance to the tested modeling methods. The TSMC 16 nm FinFET physical design occupies 0.0117 mm2, while post-layout simulation estimates 0.3089 mW at 100 MHz; no fabricated-silicon measurements are reported.

items.title: GridXAI-diffusion an adaptive graph intelligence framework for interpretable data integrity analysis in smart grid cybersecurity systems
items.summary: Smart-grid cybersecurity is increasingly challenged by sophisticated cyberattacks, evolving operational behaviors, and complex cyber-physical dependencies. Existing machine learning, deep learning, and graph-based detection methods remain limited in jointly modeling dynamic attack behaviors, spatio-temporal dependencies, attack-data scarcity, and interpretable security decisions. This study proposes GridXAI-Diffusion, an adaptive and interpretable graph intelligence framework for smart-grid cyberattack detection and data-integrity analysis. Evaluation was conducted using the Kaggle Smart Grid Security Dataset containing 1,000 samples and 24 features representing operational signals, communication behaviors, extracted characteristics, threat indicators, and attack labels. The framework integrates diffusion-based cyberattack scenario generation, dynamic cyber-physical graph construction, spatio-temporal graph transformer learning, contrastive representation learning, and Graph Temporal Causal Attention Explainability (GTCAE). The principal novelty is the coordinated integration of these established techniques into a unified cybersecurity architecture, where each component addresses attack diversity, topology-aware representation, temporal evolution, robustness, or interpretability. items.title: Readiness assessment for construction 5.0 using fuzzy logic: a case of construction organisation
items.summary: The construction industry is fast transforming to become more and more empowered by the next phase of the digital evolution, Construction 5.0, which is based on the use of new digital tools alongside human-centric, sustainable, and climate-resilient methods to address sustainability, labour shortage and climate resilience challenges. Organizational readiness for Construction 5.0 is still unclear as more technologies like AI, IoT, BIM and modular construction are being adopted, especially in developing countries such as India. Currently, this study proposes a fuzzy logic-based framework for evaluating the Construction 5.0 readiness in three major enablers, which are decomposed into seven criteria and twenty-six attributes: Resilience, Human Centricity and Environmental Sustainability. The framework is based on expert judgments from a medium-scale construction company in India, which quantifies the readiness of the enterprise using a Fuzzy Construction 5.0 Index and weak attributes by a Fuzzy Performance-Importance Index. In this single-case application, results indicate the case organisation is in the ‘Ready’ to ‘Very Ready’ range, with stronger resilience and basic human-centric practices and weaker advanced sustainability and assistive technologies. The fuzzy logic approach provides a structured, repeatable diagnostic and prioritisation roadmap to guide capability development

items.title: AnyNav: Visual neuro-symbolic friction learning for off-road navigation
items.summary: Off-road navigation is critical for a wide range of field robotics applications from planetary exploration to disaster response. However, it remains a longstanding challenge due to unstructured environments and the inherently complex terrain–vehicle interactions. Traditional physics-based methods struggle to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics underlying these interactions, while purely data-driven approaches often overfit to specific motion patterns, vehicle geometries, or platforms, limiting their generalization in diverse, real-world scenarios. To address these limitations, we introduce AnyNav, a vision-based friction estimation and navigation framework grounded in neuro-symbolic principles. Our approach integrates neural networks for visual perception with symbolic physical models for reasoning about terrain-vehicle dynamics. To enable learning in a self-supervised manner for real-world settings, we adopt the imperative learning paradigm, where a bilevel optimization framework leverages physics-based optimization for training the friction network. This explicit incorporation of physical reasoning substantially improves generalization across terrains, vehicle types, and operating conditions. items.title: EmoBench-M: Benchmarking Emotional Intelligence for Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: With the integration of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) into robotic systems and AI applications, embedding emotional intelligence (EI) capabilities is essential for enabling these models to perceive, interpret, and respond to human emotions effectively in real-world scenarios. Existing static, text-based, or text-image benchmarks overlook the multimodal complexities of real interactions and fail to capture the dynamic, context-dependent nature of emotional expressions, rendering them inadequate for evaluating MLLMs' EI capabilities. To address these limitations, we introduce EmoBench-M, a systematic benchmark grounded in established psychological theories, designed to evaluate MLLMs across 13 evaluation scenarios spanning three hierarchical dimensions: foundational emotion recognition (FER), conversational emotion understanding (CEU), and socially complex emotion analysis (SCEA). Evaluation was conducted on 27 state-of-the-art MLLMs, using both objective task-specific metrics and LLM-based evaluation, revealing a substantial performance gap relative to human-level competence. Even the best performing models, Gemini-3.0-Pro and GPT-5.2, achieve the highest scores on EmoBench-M, 70.5 and 66.5 points respectively. items.title: CoT4AD: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Explicit Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently attracted growing attention in end-to-end autonomous driving for their strong reasoning capabilities and rich world knowledge. However, existing VLAs often suffer from limited numerical reasoning ability and overly simplified input-output mappings, which hinder their performance in complex driving scenarios requiring step-by-step causal reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose CoT4AD, a novel VLA framework that introduces Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning for autonomous driving to enhance both numerical and causal reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). CoT4AD integrates visual observations and language instructions to perform semantic reasoning, scene understanding, and trajectory planning. During training, it explicitly models a perception-question-prediction-action CoT to align the reasoning space with the action space across multiple driving tasks. During inference, it performs implicit CoT reasoning to enable consistent numerical reasoning and robust decision-making in dynamic environments. Extensive experiments on both real-world and simulated benchmarks, including nuScenes and Bench2Drive, demonstrate that CoT4AD achieves state-of-the-art performance in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations. Code will be released upon paper acceptance.

items.title: Gender Bias Beyond Stereotypes: Towards Linguistically Gender-Fair Conversational LLMs
items.summary: Gender bias in NLP has mostly been studied through the lens of stereotypes, i.e. associations between gender and occupations or personality traits. In this position paper, we argue that the rise of conversational large language models (LLMs) and open-ended generation stressed another important problem that remains largely unaddressed: masculine generics bias. In many languages, including German, French or Spanish, masculine forms are used to refer to mixed-gender groups or to people whose gender is unknown or non-binary (masculine generics, or MG for short). Decades of psycholinguistic research show that these forms are not interpreted as truly generic and instead lead people to have more male-centric mental representations. As LLMs are adopted by an ever-growing number of users worldwide for a wide range of tasks, this bias can now be perpetuated in everyday interactions, all the more since preliminary studies already show that LLMs lean heavily on MG and are reluctant to use gender-fair language spontaneously. We review the evidence for why it matters, explain why existing mitigation approaches are not enough for conversational LLMs, show that GFL in German, French and Spanish is lacking in LLM pre-training corpora, and outline 6 research directions towards building multilingual, linguistically gender-fair conversational LLMs.

items.title: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
items.summary: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching. This method integrates novel retrieval mechanisms, including LLM-based, vector-based, graph traversal-based, and hybrid techniques with advanced reranking schemes to extract the most relevant subgraphs from large external KGs. Our approach achieves superior results without requiring re-training, as evidenced by improvements of 39.79% in precision and 30.56% in F1 score over LLM-based state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods (e.g., Jellyfish-8B) on the MIMIC dataset, and enhancements of 69.20% in precision and 21.99% in F1 score over pre-trained language model (PLM)-based SOTA methods (e.g., SMAT) on the Synthea dataset. Additionally, KG-RAG4SM scales effectively across KGs from commonsense KGs to domain-specific ones, while its instruction-tuning knowledge exclusion component ensures truthful performance in end-to-end schema matching tasks despite the suboptimal relevance of KG context. items.title: Enhancing Neural Code Representation With Additional Context
items.summary: Automated program comprehension underpins many software engineering tasks, from code summarisation to clone detection. While recent deep learning models have achieved strong results, they typically rely on source code alone and overlook other information that developers routinely use to understand programs, such as version history or structural relationships. This gap limits the ability of current models to capture the broader context in which code evolves and operates. To address this, we conduct an empirical study of how enriching code representations with these additional contextual signals affects the performance of neural models on key program comprehension tasks. To ensure a robust comparison, we fine-tune five foundational code models (tree-based and pre-trained Transformer architectures), namely CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, CodeT5, PLBART, and ASTNN, under both code-only and context-augmented settings. items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Structure-Aware Numerical Reasoning in LLaMA 3.1–8B
items.summary: Recent work has shown that large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong numerical sequence modeling capabilities and show promise in time-series prediction. While LLMs display in-context learning capabilities, the mechanisms with which they accomplish time-series prediction remain unclear. Specifically, whether they truly understand the underlying structure, which at a minimum requires reasoning over first differences in the sequence of numbers. To study this, we investigate Llama 3.1-8B from a mechanistic interpretability point of view. Specifically, we sample n random numbers and repeat them with an offset. We find that Llama displays strong performance on our tasks suggesting that it can pick up on the underlying structure.
